facts.text: Princeton was named after Reverend Thomas Prince, pastor of Boston’s Old South Church and one of the town’s first proprietors.
Mount Wachusett, the town’s most prominent peak, straddles Princeton and Westminster but its main entrance lies within Princeton.
The town’s public library, founded in 1884, has served residents for over a century and still stands as a community hub.
In 1675, Mary Rowlandson was ransomed at Redemption Rock, a historic site now inside Princeton, during King Philip’s War.
The 2001 comedy Shallow Hal filmed several scenes on Wachusett Mountain, giving Princeton a brief moment in Hollywood.
Princeton’s East Princeton Village Historic District is one of five sites listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving the town’s 19th‑century architecture.
